So, Paul was motivated by multiple reasons to spread his religious ideas. One explanation is that he was a Roman agent tasked with destroying Judaism from within, using Jesus as a messiah of peace to undermine Jewish war efforts. Another perspective suggests Paul might have been a Jewish spy working for the Romans by spreading Jewish faith. I believe both explanations are valid; Paul likely had a calling to create his own religious empire and saw an opportunity to achieve personal power through religion.

God and Satan's argument in the joke illustrates how Paul transformed Jesus' message into a tool for building his empire, just as Ray Croc turned McDonald's into a global franchise. Paul succeeded by convincing small business owners to invest in his church model, promising wealth and paradise. Similarly, Croc spread the gospel of wealth through his franchises.

Paul’s strategy involved creating debate among Jews, weakening their resolve, and spiritually enslaving people to work harder for him. He pitched this idea to Roman patriarchs, emphasizing division within the Jewish diaspora and the conversion of some to reduce overall conflict against them. To Jewish leaders, he proposed spreading faith to Gentiles, elevating their status as a chosen people and making Torah divine.

Paul’s message was simple: obedience, no circumcision required, and urgency due to Jesus' imminent return. This pitch resonated with many who followed him into Christianity, aligning the interests of Jews and Romans through shared religious goals. Augustine came after the Catholic Church became the official religion of the Roman Empire, continuing Paul's legacy by providing theological justification for its dominance.
